Job Description: **Job Description**

Hope Flynn is seeking an Art Teaching Assistant to support a series of children's paint bynumber workshops at the Burlington Public Library, New Appleby Branch.

The Art Teaching Assistant will assist children ages 6 to 13 during the workshops by providing encouragement, answering questions, preparing materials, and helping create a welcoming and inclusive learning environment.

Schedule

This is a contract position for four workshops.

**Workshop Dates:**

* August 9
* August 23
* August 30
* September 5

Workshops are held on weekends from approximately **2:00 pm to 4:00 pm.** at the Burlington Public Library, New Appleby Branch.

Compensation

Compensation is **$120 per workshop**, which includes a **$20 travel reimbursement**.

Responsibilities

* Assist with setting up and cleaning up before and after each workshop.
* Prepare and organize art supplies and materials.
* Support children ages 6 to 13 during paint by number activities.
* Answer participant questions and provide one\-on\-one assistance when needed.
* Help maintain a welcoming, organized, and inclusive workshop environment.
* Work collaboratively with the workshop instructor throughout each session.

Qualifications

* Friendly, reliable, and professional.
* Enjoy working with children.
* Interest in art or arts education.
* Experience working with children, camps, schools, or community art programs is considered an asset.
* Ability to communicate clearly and work well as part of a team.

Application Requirements

Please submit a resume. An art portfolio is optional but welcomed.

Only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Pay: $50\.00 per hour

Work Location: In person

**The Research Coordinator I will work closely with Dr. Hwang’s team to support new and ongoing evaluation research projects with a focus on interventions to address complex problems and improve health and social conditions for people who are unhoused. **Prepare and submit Research Ethics Board (REB) applications, amendments, approvals and staff updates**

**Experience with evaluation theory, frameworks and methodologies**

Job Description: **Status:** Regular Full\-time (Mon, Tue and Wed are on\-site days. Hybrid is optional for Thurs or Fri)

  


The Sunnybrook Research Institute is seeking a Full\-time **Research Assistant** to assist Dr. Natalie Coburn with several large, multi\-center collaborative research projects, databases and educational projects. This individual will be joining our established research program of clinical epidemiologists, clinicians, qualitative researchers and pharmaco\-economists examining clinical outcomes, resource utilization, patient\-reported outcomes and costs of cancer patients within Ontario.

  


The successful candidate will be responsible for providing management of subsets of research projects, while keeping track of deadlines and performing general research administrative tasks.

  


**Key Responsibilities Related to Research Project**


* Organize and analyze Delphi consensus panel.
* Manage trans\-Provincial database.
* Manage scoping reviews.
* Support ongoing patient and provider education efforts.
* Coordinate Canadian Gastric Cancer Association (CaGCA) conference and newsletters.
* Provide additional support for other quantitative and qualitative studies, as needed.

  




**General Research Assistant Duties**


* Prepare REB applications and renewals.
* Prepare annual grant reports, including budget summaries.
* Coordinate team meetings, prepare materials and agendas and produce and distribute minutes.
* Coordinate with project stakeholders to meet project timelines and deliverables.
* Assistance with ongoing research projects
* Other tasks to assist in ongoing research of the team, as appropriate.

  




**Skills and Qualifications**


* Bachelor’s degree in health services related discipline. A master’s degree is an asset.
* Previous qualitative or quantitative research experience preferred, including REB applications, analysis of large population\-based databases, patient interviews/education.
* Previous experience interviewing cancer patients or similar experience.
* Attention to detail and organization.
* Ability to work closely as a team and provide assistance to support team members.
* Ability to work with minimal supervision while achieving specific goals within specific timeframes.
* Time management skills to manage and prioritize workload and timelines.
* Flexibility and ability to work under tight deadlines.
* Multitasking
* Strong verbal and written communication skills
* Willing and able to rapidly learn new tasks.
* Mon, Tue and Wed are on\-site days (Hybrid is optional for Thurs or Fri)

  




**Please send a cover letter and curriculum vitae in one PDF document**

  

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.
